assignedTask.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
assignedTask.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

opportunities.title: Claude Code setup: CLAUDE.md, permissions, hooks, MCP servers
opportunities.excerpt:
Commit the project context as CLAUDE.md and configure agents safely for a malware-adjacent repo.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` at repo root with the REX project context (hard rules, stack, layout, phases, unresolved decisions, working rules)
- [ ] `.claude/settings.json` (committed): deny reading/executing sample/quarantine dirs and real artifact fixtures; deny `curl|wget` to arbitrary hosts; allow common read-only commands
- [ ] Hook that blocks executing any file under sample/quarantine paths (rule: never run unknown samples on host)
- [ ] `.mcp.json` (committed, no secrets) listing project MCP servers; secrets via env only
- [ ] MCP servers: **GitHub** (issues/PRs; currently failing auth - fix token), **Postgres** read-only against local dev DB only, **Playwright/browser** for apps/web E2E; optional docs MCP for library docs
- [ ] No MCP server gets access to object storage, artifact samples, provider keys or worker credentials (rules 1, 9)
- [ ] Plugins documented: superpowers (process skills), ponytail (see tool-ponytail)
- [ ] `.claude/settings.local.json` git-ignored

opportunities.title: security(mcp): the `dir` argument can relocate the memory store anywhere on the host
opportunities.excerpt:
**Severity:** medium · **Control:** CWE-22-adjacent, CWE-862 · Agentic ASI02

## Evidence
`src/mcp.ts` `resolveStoreForRequest` takes `a.dir || a.workspace || a.project_dir || a.cwd` and calls `findOrCreateProjectRoot(dir)` with no comparison against the configured workspace root; `src/root.ts` then `mkdirSync`/`writeFileSync` the store in place (no `mode`, so 0755/0644 under a default umask). Contrast the control that *is* implemented for sync pools: `src/sync/pool.ts` confines `pool_dir` with `resolveWithin` and creates it `0o700`.

## Impact
Any client — a remote token holder or a prompt-injected agent — can point the server at another project's or user's directory, read or poison that store, and create `.memory/` at an arbitrary path with world-readable permissions.

## Fix
Resolve `dir` and reject anything outside the configured workspace root (reuse `resolveWithin`); require explicit operator opt-in for cross-root access. Create store directories `0o700` and files `0o600`.

Source: audit 2026-11-26 (S7).

opportunities.title: security(mcp): prompt and resource output is not marked as data (indirect prompt injection)
opportunities.excerpt:
**Severity:** low-medium (architectural) · **Control:** OWASP LLM01 2026 (Prompt Injection, now explicitly including memory persistence), Agentic ASI01/ASI06

## Evidence
`src/prompts.ts` substitutes `{{current_constraints}}` with raw CURRENT.md text; `src/mcp/prompts.ts` returns it as a `role: "user"` text block with no data envelope. `src/mcp/resources.ts` returns raw CURRENT.md/entry JSON. The repo already has the control — `src/security/context_sanitizer.ts` `wrapAgentContext`/`sanitizeContextForAgent` — but it is applied at only one agent-facing call site.

## Impact
Any write path (`memory_import`, a sync packet, an agent note, a hand-edited YAML mirror) can place instruction-shaped text that later arrives as a first-class user prompt with no delimiter, so a downstream model cannot distinguish data from instructions. Prompt *arguments* cannot break the template (single-pass rendering), so this is content-channel injection.

## Fix
Run `wrapAgentContext` over `getMcpPrompt`/`readMcpResource` output, or fence memory-derived sections with an explicit data delimiter and strip the delimiter from content before rendering.

Source: audit 2026-11-26 (S9); OWASP LLM Top 10 2026-08-03, LLM01.

opportunities.title: [BUG] Claude Code does not detect, warn about, or protect against external programs overwriting behavior settings and user hooks in settings.json
opportunities.excerpt:
# [BUG] Claude Code does not detect, warn about, or protect against external programs overwriting behavior settings and user hooks in settings.json

## Environment
- Product: Claude Code desktop app (Code tab), macOS
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)
- Date: 2026-10-19
- Related: #103322 (memory rules added without a consistency check against existing rules). Same root cause: incoming configuration is never checked against the existing context.

## Symptoms
1. A session auto-compacted at 49% context. The user never changed the compaction threshold.
2. The cause was `env.CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE = "50"` written into `~/.claude/settings.json` by a third-party npm package (DietCode 0.5.0). The default compaction point for a 1M model (about 967K tokens) silently became about 500K.
3. The same package rewrites `hooks.UserPromptSubmit`, `hooks.PostToolUse`, `hooks.PreCompact`, and `statusLine` in settings.json wholesale once a day. Any hook the user registered on those events (this user relies on a UserPromptSubmit hook that injects their working rules) can be deleted without warning.
4. Claude Code reads this file every session, yet it never told the user that the compaction threshold changed or that the hook list changed. The user only found the cause after compaction had already happened.
5. The app's usage report showed the auto-compact point for this session as 97%. In reality the 50% override was in effect and compaction happened at 49%. The displayed value did not match actual behavior.

## Why this is critical
- settings.json controls Claude Code's behavior (compaction point, hooks, permissions, environment variables). Behavior changes without the user knowing who changed what.
- When a hook that enforces the user's rules silently disappears, the user keeps working believing the rules are still applied.
- Compaction irreversibly summarizes the earlier part of the conversation. Unintended early compaction means lost working context.

## Expected behavior
- At session start, if any behavior-affecting key in settings.json (env, hooks, permissions, statusLine, etc.) changed since the last session, show what changed and ask for confirmation.
- Warn when a user-registered hook has disappeared.
- The usage report should show the auto-compact point actually in effect, including `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Register a user
